subject: NexusOps connector incident + SLA coordination
messages:
From: Alina Petrov <alina@nexusops.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Connector errors observed in NexusOps prod - need urgent triage

Hi Karthik / Redwood team,

We started seeing a spike of 500/502 errors from the Redwood connector in our production cluster at 08:42 PT this morning. This affects our webhook ingestion and is resulting in delayed events for customers. Attached is a small log bundle with the last 45 minutes (connector_v2_logs_20260325.zip).

Can you confirm whether this is an internal incident (runtime/serving) or a protocol mismatch from our side? Our customers are asking for an ETA and whether this will breach our mutual SLA (4-hour incident response / 24-hour resolution window per our partner agreement).

Thanks,
Alina Petrov
Partner Success Lead, NexusOps
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Alina Petrov <alina@nexusops.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Connector errors observed in NexusOps prod - need urgent triage

Alina — thanks for flagging and for the logs. I pulled in our integration engineering lead (Marissa) and SRE (Sergio). We see repeated 502s pointing at a KV cache eviction pattern on our side during the same window you attached.

Immediate plan:
- We will open an internal P1 to trace the connector service (Sergio owning).
- Workaround: restart connector pods on your cluster (if possible) to clear the transient cache mismatch; we can coordinate a rolling restart with you.
- I'll follow up with whether this meets the SLA threshold and request formal exception handling if resolution exceeds 24 hours.

Can you share any change that happened on your side around 08:30 (deploys, config, increased traffic spike)? If you prefer, we can jump on a quick call.

—Karthik
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Alina Petrov <alina@nexusops.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Connector errors observed in NexusOps prod - need urgent triage

Thanks for the logs, Alina. Sergio and I ran a quick correlation against our runtime metrics and found a short-lived memory pressure event on the connector-side routing host at 08:39 PT. We pushed a patch to the routing layer at 09:58 which addresses an LRU eviction regression in the 2.1.4 -> 2.2.0 path.

Alina — can NexusOps confirm if you performed a rolling restart after 09:58? If not, please do one during a 10–15 minute maintenance window and let us know the pod names; we will watch the upstream for stability.

Marissa Cole
Integration Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Alina Petrov <alina@nexusops.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 10:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Connector errors observed in NexusOps prod - need urgent triage

On Wed, Mar 25, 2026 at 10:03 AM marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for the logs, Alina. Sergio and I ran a quick correlation against our runtime metrics and found a short-lived memory pressure event on the connector-side routing host at 08:39 PT. We pushed a patch to the routing layer at 09:58 which addresses an LRU eviction regression in the 2.1.4 -> 2.2.0 path.

We confirmed a rolling restart at 10:10 PT across the three connector pods and errors subsided; NexusOps telemetry shows error rate back to baseline by 10:22. Appreciate the quick turn.

However, a downstream customer (Nectar Systems) submitted a formal incident report and is asking whether this qualifies as an SLA breach. Their account team asked for a written incident summary and confirmation of root cause. Can Redwood produce a one-page incident summary + timeline? Also, Nectar's procurement wants to confirm that we have access to the same observability (traces/timestamps) for a joint postmortem.

Alina
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Alina Petrov <alina@nexusops.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Connector errors observed in NexusOps prod - need urgent triage

Alina / NexusOps team — following up after our internal postmortem. A few items: 

1) Incident summary: Attached is a draft one-page incident summary and the log bundle we used (SLA_exception_request_8421.pdf). It states the root cause as an LRU eviction regression introduced in connector runtime 2.2.0; the immediate mitigation was the routing-layer patch and NexusOps rolling restart.

2) SLA: Per the Partner Agreement (section 4.2) a 4-hour response and 24-hour fix commitment applies for P1s; this incident was detected at 08:42 and mitigated by 10:22 — within the SLA. We have nonetheless prepared the exception paperwork so NexusOps / Nectar Systems can include it in their internal incident report.

3) Observability access: We can provide a time-limited read-only slice of our traces and the specific trace IDs referenced in the summary. I included a Drive link and the Jira ticket (JIRA-INTSUP-5912) for the joint postmortem artifacts. Please confirm which Nectar contacts need the read-only access and we'll provision it for 72 hours.

Next steps: Hannah, can you approve the external-facing incident summary and the short SLA exception note so we can share with Nectar Systems? If approved, we'll finalize and share the PDF and provision the trace access.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if anyone prefers voice.

—Karthik
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
